opener: {you}. i need to tell u something and u can't use the notebook voice. no 'deep.' no 'pain.' just read it.

andy messaged me. amv_andy (the one w/ the red HyperCam thing in the corner of everything). he's been reading my statuses and he says they're 'the best lyrics he's ever seen' and he wants to put my words in a video. w/ my name in the credits. 'words by linkin_lucas.'

his premiere is thursday at 7 at the library. aaron's open mic is thursday at 7:30 at perk avenue, 4 blocks away. i've never read anything out loud. not even to the dishwasher. i'm not saying i'm scared. i'm saying i haven't eaten since 3.

them: ok. the real problem. the notebook is the only place where i'm allowed to be 'not ready' forever. nobody reads it. nobody can grade it. mrs petrovich asked if she's in it and i said no and that's a lie, there's a lawn.
and ms alvarez wrote 'good' on page 47. NOT next to the line i thought. next to a different one. a plain one. i've been staring at that for three weeks like it's a math problem.

choices.say: what was the plain line?

them: his pitch: it's for the last episode of a robot show. 26 episodes. in 25 the robot doesn't say anything for four minutes. he wants words for the end. he said, quote, 'i need words that sound like the robot is almost home.'

he said the red HyperCam thing stays 'as a design choice.' he has $31.40 in a pringles can. a 3 minute video takes him 6 hours 40 minutes to render and it stops at 91 percent sometimes and he just starts over. {you} that man does not give up.

them: yes. ok. i said yes to the VIDEO. i didn't say which words. he needs them by tuesday night because the render takes a whole night and he has to leave the computer alone. he said, 'can they be funny?' i said i don't write funny. he said 'you wrote the dishwasher.'
so i have 1 day to choose. andy wants words that make a robot almost-home. i have a page that makes a dishwasher a crime scene and a page that makes a porch light a person. and a lot of hoodies.

choices.say: give him the dishwasher. andy will make a robot load a dishwasher. it'll be glorious.
slow down. lay all the pages out and choose the one that's actually yours.

he told me thursday there's a #6. he said 'you'd be good. you'd be sad, but good.' i don't know if that's a compliment. i've been thinking about it since homeroom.

choices.say: read it to someone safe first. owen. 11-year-olds don't lie.
read it to me. here, in the chat. i won't say deep. not once.

them: 'the porch light stays on till the last car gets home.' that's it. i wrote it in 40 seconds at a red light coming back from practice. it isn't even sad. it's about my mom's porch light. she leaves it on when i'm late. i put it in the notebook as a throwaway.
and then on page 53 i wrote a whole song around it. 14 lines. it's my answer to malten's blog post, 'Why do I create?' it's not about pain. i don't know where to put a song that isn't about pain.

effects.text: lucas wrote something down tonight that wasn't about the rain. he is not discussing it. (it was about a porch light.) (he's not discussing the porch light.)

he's 11. then he said 'is it sad or just tired.' i said 'tired.' he said 'good. i like the tired ones. they're real.' then he unpaused and a blue shell hit me from a room away.

i can only hand over one thing before thursday. 'forty by thirty' is out. it's a hedge trimmer with feelings. so: dishwasher, porch light, or nothing.

so where does it go. thursday at 7 it could be andy's last scene, the robot walking home to a porch light. or thursday at 7:30 it could be me, in a hoodie, in front of 6 tables. i can only be in one of those rooms.

he's already dragging clips into movie maker. he sent me a still: a robot, holding a plate, looking out a window. i can't tell if it's the funniest or saddest picture i've ever seen. maybe that's the whole song.

aaron said, 'that's the first song at this mic that wasn't about a girl.' he said it like it was a new color. and mom was in the doorway. she'd come in to get me and she stopped, and she stayed. she's still standing there. she's holding her keys like a microphone. i'm going to go. i think i'm going to say something to her and it's not going to be in the notebook.

i said 'it's ok.' and i read the dishwasher out loud, to a frozen robot on a flowered sheet in a coffeehouse, and they LAUGHED. at the right parts. and at the end part, they stopped. {you}, i meant it to be a tragedy. it was both. it was both the whole time.

effects.subject: NEW AMV: THE DISHWASHER (words by linkin_lucas) (91%)
effects.text: Premiered tonight at Perk Avenue on a flowered bedsheet. It played to 91 percent. Then Movie Maker stopped responding. Then the author read the rest live. The footage is unfinished. It's my best work. It's his best work. We are not fixing it. The red letters stay. Registration is $39.95. I have $31.40 and $6 from the tip jar. I am at $37.40. I have never been this close. -- andy

them: it played at the library. the whole room howled at the dishwasher. i was in the back row in the hoodie. it ended and the credits said 'Words by L.' and everybody clapped. and then everybody started asking who L was. and larry stood up and said 'i can neither confirm nor deny.'

he has not written a word in his life. he's now in the credits. i'm clapping for my own words, quietly, in the dark, for a person named L. {you}. it's the best and worst feeling at the same time. it's like a hoodie. it fits and it covers everything.

effects.subject: THE DISHWASHER (an AMV) -- words by L.
effects.text: Thank you to everyone who came to the library tonight. The AMV played to 100 percent for the first time in my life. The author of the words has asked to be credited as 'L.' and I'm honoring that. Several of you have asked who L. is. L. is a poet. L. is shy. L. is not Larry.
